name: Swagnet
tagline: Enterprise swag that ships itself. No closet. No leftover hoodies in a size nobody wants.
positioning: Usage-based swag infrastructure for companies that give away too much branded stuff and can't account for a single unit of it.

hero.h1: Your swag budget is a black hole. We built the flashlight.
hero.sub: Swagnet is on-demand branded merch for enterprises. Store nothing, print on ship, and pay per item that actually leaves the building. Every unit tracked, coded, and defensible in a board deck.

features.title: Kill the swag closet
features.description: No pallets in a spare conference room. Products print the moment someone claims them, so you stop paying storage on 400 XL vests you'll never move.

features.title: One SKU, 40 warehouses
features.description: A single catalog fulfills from the closest node worldwide. Field marketing in Munich and Ops in Austin pull from the same brand kit without a customs headache.

features.title: Spend you can defend
features.description: Every item ships with a cost code, owner, and event tag. Finance gets a per-unit ledger instead of a shoebox of vendor invoices.

features.title: Send-to-anyone links
features.description: Drop a claim link in an email and recipients pick size, color, and address themselves. No spreadsheet of shirt sizes. Ever again.

features.title: Reorder is a myth
features.description: There are no minimum order quantities because there are no orders. You never reprint a run and eat 600 units of a discontinued logo.

testimonials.quote: We used to expense $180k a year in swag and could account for maybe half of it. Swagnet turned it into a per-unit line item my CFO stopped flagging. The hoodies also don't smell like a storage unit anymore.
testimonials.name: Priya Ramanathan

testimonials.quote: I ran 22 field events last quarter without printing a single box in advance. Everything shipped to the venue the week of. My garage is empty for the first time in three years.
testimonials.name: Deacon Whitfield

testimonials.quote: The claim links alone paid for the contract. Onboarding used to mean chasing new hires for shirt sizes in Slack. Now it's a link in the offer letter and I never touch it.
testimonials.name: Mara Kellenbach
